suzanne-giesemann:
Suzanne Giesemann spent the first part of her working life as a US Navy officer. She reached the rank of Commander, served as a commanding officer and, at the Joint Chiefs of Staff, was aide to its Chairman; she also earned a master's degree in National Security Affairs. Her memoir Messages of Hope, and the documentary that shares its title, follow her path from the military to mediumship, and a second documentary, based on her book Wolf's Message, appeared in 2025.

Today she works as an evidential medium, spiritual teacher and author. Alongside evidential mediumship she teaches The Awakened Way, her name for living in conscious connection with higher guidance, and she passes on channelled messages from a group of guides known as Sanaya. Her practices include the BLESS ME Method, a way of connecting with higher consciousness, and a brief meditation called the SIP of the Divine. Among her more than a dozen books are The Awakened Way, Making the Afterlife Connection and Always Connected. Students can learn through self-paced video courses at her own school and on The Shift Network, and she also offers a free app of daily messages, a live gathering each month, Hemi-Sync recordings and a sizeable YouTube channel.
robert-moss:
Born in Australia, Robert Moss is a storyteller, author and dream teacher who created Active Dreaming, his own blend of shamanic practice and modern dreamwork. He had three near-death experiences as a child; he sees them as his first openings to other realms, and he later wrote about them in a memoir. He once taught ancient history as a lecturer at the Australian National University, and has also worked as a journalist, poet and independent scholar.

In Active Dreaming, dreams are approached as real experiences and journeys rather than simply as material for analysis. Moss teaches how to re-enter a dream, how to travel consciously in dreams and how to share them in small groups, as well as kairomancy, his word for noticing signs and synchronicity in waking life. Conscious Dreaming, Dreamgates, The Secret History of Dreaming, Sidewalk Oracles and Growing Big Dreams are among his more than a dozen books. He gives workshops around the world, offers a three-year training for those who want to teach Active Dreaming, and has recorded many self-paced courses with The Shift Network on lucid and shamanic dreaming, ancient dream traditions, and dreams of death and the afterlife.
helen-liang:
Master Helen Liang has taught Tai Chi, Qigong and the Chinese internal martial arts for more than thirty years. Her training began in China in 1976, and through her father, Grandmaster Shou-Yu Liang, she is a direct inheritor of the Emei Wushu lineage. She serves as vice president of the family's school in Richmond, near Vancouver, Canada (the SYL Wushu Taiji Qigong Institute), and two international Wushu organisations have ranked her at 8th degree.

Her repertoire includes the 24, 13-posture and 8-posture Tai Chi forms, Liu He Ba Fa (Water Style), a flowing internal art, as well as Qigong and a philosophy of the martial arts grounded in Yin and Yang and the Yi Jing. Together with her father she wrote and presented a 130-episode Tai Chi instruction series for Canadian television, and she has produced many teaching videos for YMAA. She is patient and thorough as a teacher, dividing each form into clear stages and paying close attention to alignment, breathing and a calm, focused mind. Classes run at the institute and online, and The Shift Network carries several of her self-paced courses in Tai Chi and Liu He Ba Fa.
cyndi-dale:
Based in Minnesota, Cyndi Dale is an American author, teacher and intuitive energy healer. After studying English and philosophy she undertook master's-level study in divinity at Bethel University, and she has trained in Therapeutic Touch, shamanism, intuitive healing and the Lakota Way. Across several decades she has worked one to one with tens of thousands of clients in private intuitive sessions and given workshops in the Americas, Europe, Africa and China.

The subtle body is at the heart of her teaching: an expanded system of twelve chakras, the auric fields, kundalini and the energetic boundaries that lie between people. Her more than 40 books have appeared in some 20 languages; among them Energetic Boundaries, Llewellyn's Complete Book of Chakras and The Subtle Body, her encyclopedia of energetic anatomy. She offers self-paced video courses on The Shift Network as well as her own online classes, audio programmes and small in-person retreats, combining clear explanation with guided meditation and practical exercises for working with energy and developing intuition.
elayne-kalila-doughty:
Elayne Kalila Doughty teaches the mysteries of the Divine Feminine. She holds a master's degree, trained as a marriage and family therapist, and has been ordained as a priestess in two lineages: the Avalonian 13 Moon Mystery School and the Rosa Mystica Mystery School. Earlier in her life she wrote and directed theatre with prison inmates and ran programmes for women facing hardship. The Priestess Presence Temple, an online sisterhood she founded in 2014, now numbers tens of thousands of women.

Through the Priestess Presence mystery schools, which she founded and leads as dean, she trains and ordains women as modern-day priestesses, working with ritual, ceremony, archetypes, shadow work and embodied practice. Mary Magdalene is a central figure in her recent teaching, together with the myrrhophores, the lineages of scent-priestesses who anointed with holy oils. Her offerings include self-paced courses, year-long online initiations, retreats and pilgrimages; she also hosts The RED Podcast and created the Magdalene Rose Oracle deck. Some of her Magdalene courses can be found on The Shift Network.
philip-carr-gomm:
Philip Carr-Gomm, an English psychologist, writer and teacher of Druidry, lives on the South Downs in Sussex. As a teenager he studied Druidry with Ross Nichols, who had founded OBOD, the Druid order he would later lead. Asked to take it on in 1988, he guided it for more than thirty years while it grew into one of the world's largest Druid groups. He studied psychology at University College London, went on to train in psychosynthesis psychotherapy, play therapy, sophrology and Montessori education, and later qualified to teach mindfulness meditation and Yoga Nidra.

In his teaching, nature spirituality meets Western psychology and the broader perennial wisdom tradition. He works through conversation, storytelling, poetry, ritual, meditation and oracles drawn from plants and animals. Of the twenty or so books he has written or co-written, the best known include Druid Mysteries and The Book of English Magic, along with two decks made with his wife Stephanie, The DruidCraft Tarot and The Druid Animal Oracle. He offers online courses through his own platforms and The Shift Network, gives talks and workshops, presents the long-running YouTube series Tea with a Druid, and founded the Sophrology Institute.
penelope-smith:
An American teacher, Penelope Smith has worked professionally as an animal communicator since the 1970s, and it was she who named the field 'interspecies telepathic communication'. She holds degrees in the social sciences at both bachelor's and master's level, and trained in human counselling and holistic bodywork before making a profession of the ability to understand animals that she had had all her life. Many of today's professional animal communicators started with her courses, and her students know her as the grandmother of interspecies communication.

Her view is that every person is born able to communicate mind to mind with other species, and that presence, receptivity and practice can bring this ability back. Three of her books have become classics of the field: Animals in Spirit, on how animals experience death and the afterlife, along with Animal Talk and When Animals Speak. She founded and edited the magazine Species Link, drew up a code of ethics for animal communicators in 1990, and set up the Animal Communicators Coalition for Animal Welfare. Private consultations are no longer part of her work; she teaches instead through online courses, some of them on The Shift Network, as well as audio courses and recorded seminars.
wendy-de-rosa:
Working with sensitive and empathic people, Wendy De Rosa teaches, writes and practises as an intuitive energy healer. At the School of Intuitive Studies, which she founded, her year-long Energy Healing and Intuition Training shows students how to read and clear their own energy system through the chakras, build their intuition and work as intuitive healers themselves. She also has a podcast, The Wendy De Rosa Sessions, and runs The Sanctuary, a monthly membership offering live group healings and meditations.

Grounding and energetic boundaries are central to her teaching, as are the four intuitive pathways of clairvoyance, clairaudience, claircognizance and clairsentience, which she teaches through guided practice rather than through theory alone. Her books are Expanding Your Heart: Awakening Through Four Stages of a Spiritual Opening, Becoming an Empowered Empath and Energy Healing Through the Chakras. She has taught at Kripalu, Omega and Blue Spirit, and The Shift Network has hosted many of her live and self-paced courses for empaths.
roger-jahnke:
Dr. Roger Jahnke, a doctor of Chinese medicine and a teacher of tai chi and qigong, has practised acupuncture and traditional Chinese medicine clinically for more than three decades and has made ten research and cultural journeys to China. In 2000 he set up IIQTC, his Institute of Integral Qigong and Tai Chi, based in Santa Barbara, California, and he remains its director and lead trainer. Thousands of qigong and tai chi teachers and practice leaders have trained with the institute and its faculty, today mostly through modular certification online.

He calls his approach Integral Qigong: a combination of gentle movement, breath practice, self-applied massage and meditation. He also created Tai Chi Easy, a simplified practice intended for beginners and for community classes. His books are The Healer Within and The Healing Promise of Qi, the latter drawing on more than twenty forms of qigong and tai chi, both traditional and modern. He has taught at Esalen, Omega and other centres, and offers live and self-paced programmes on The Shift Network.
jeffrey-thompson:
Dr. Jeffrey Thompson trained as a chiropractor and has a fine-arts background in music, and for several decades he has studied the effects of sound, rhythm and vibration on awareness and brainwave states. A composer, sound researcher and teacher, he founded the Center for Neuroacoustic Research, based in Carlsbad, California. His neuroacoustic soundtracks rely on brainwave entrainment, using phase-modulated binaural beats of his own design and three-dimensional sound processing, and he worked on the release of NASA's Voyager space-sound recordings.

Scientific Sounds sells his recordings for relaxation, meditation and creativity, and Sounds True has published several of his audio programmes, among them Brainwave Symphony and Gamma Meditation System. His YouTube channel carries long-form live talks on intuition, consciousness, sacred geometry and the default mode network, as well as Global Mind Link, his group sound sessions. On The Shift Network he teaches quantum acoustics and psychoacoustics.
martha-collard:
Martha Collard is a gong master who founded Red Doors Studio in Wong Chuk Hang, Hong Kong, a space dedicated to Kundalini yoga, labyrinth walking and meditation gongs. Her route there ran through three decades of management consulting: she became the youngest partner anywhere at TASA, a Swiss executive search firm, and in 1992 started a consultancy of her own. When the Yoga Society of Hong Kong was formed, she became its first chairman.

Her main teacher was Gong Master Don Conreaux. She has also studied voice with Chanara Richmond, overtoning with Mark van Tongeren, integral sound at the Svaram Sound Institute and flumie (friction mallet) playing with Bear Love, as well as singing bowls. Gong trainings at Red Doors are small and hands-on and run in three levels, moving from playing for oneself to leading sessions for others and playing with fellow musicians; she also teaches in New York and around Asia. Online, she teaches gong playing and gong meditation on The Shift Network and offers free livestreams at each New Moon. She has given talks at TEDx Hong Kong and the Global Wellness Summit.
ramsay-taum:
Kumu Ramsay Taum, a Native Hawaiian cultural practitioner and teacher, founded the Life Enhancement Institute of the Pacific. Trained and mentored by respected kūpuna (elders), he practises and teaches hoʻoponopono, the Hawaiian process of forgiveness and reconciliation, along with lomi haha (body alignment) and the Hawaiian martial art Kaihewalu Lua. After his schooling at The Kamehameha Schools he spent time at the US Air Force Academy, and he later earned a public administration degree at the University of Southern California.

As a speaker, adviser and facilitator he brings Hawaiian values such as aloha, pono and kuleana into business, tourism, planning and community life. He offers hoʻoponopono sessions for groups and individuals, in-person immersions in Lua, hoʻoponopono and the Aloha Way, and talks for conferences, churches and TEDx. His course on The Shift Network, The Sacred Path of Aloha, covers hoʻoponopono, HA breathing, chant, ceremony and ancestral remembrance.
david-crow:
For more than 40 years David Crow has worked in natural medicine as an American herbalist, acupuncturist, aromatherapist and author. He was one of the first Westerners licensed in Chinese medicine after training in it, and he studied Ayurvedic and Tibetan medicine through traditional internships in India and Nepal. In Search of the Medicine Buddha, his book about those Himalayan years, describes his studies with Tibetan physicians and meditation teachers. He founded Floracopeia, which produces essential oils and botanical products in partnership with small-scale growers and distillers worldwide, and his ethnobotanical research has taken him far afield.

In David's teaching, knowledge of plants is joined with meditation and ecological spirituality. His courses explore the chakras and the inner landscape of the body through yogic and Tibetan traditions, the craft of blending essential oils, and a heart-centred meditation that follows the rhythm of the heartbeat. He has taught for more than 25 years in Europe, Canada and the United States. Since 2015 he has taught regularly on The Shift Network, where he founded and hosted the yearly Plant Medicine Summit. He lives in Grass Valley, California, and now teaches mostly online.
puma-fredy-quispe-singona:
From Chinchero, near Cusco in Peru, Puma Fredy Quispe Singona is an Andean medicine carrier who keeps the Rainbow Lineage traditions of his village's Inca people. When he was six he was struck by lightning, and afterwards his grandfather, the late Don Maximo, took him on for training. He has also studied the huachuma lineages of the Peruvian coast and the ayahuasca lineage of the Shipibo people in the Amazon. Since he was 15 he has spoken at international gatherings, and he has led meetings for spiritual leaders and young Indigenous leaders.

Andean cosmology, ceremony and the mesa, the portable altar of the Andes, are at the centre of his teaching, always grounded in deep respect for Pachamama. In Chinchero he founded the Noqan Kani Global Community Center, a place where locals and visitors can learn Andean ways and nature-based wisdom, and he runs his online mesa programmes from there. He is a co-founder of Pumadventures, which takes groups to Peru's sacred sites, and on The Shift Network he has taught many self-paced courses on Andean shamanic practice, spirit animals and the Chakana, or Andean cross.
banafsheh-sayyad:
Born in Iran into a family of performing artists, Banafsheh Sayyad is a Persian sacred dancer, choreographer and teacher. In 2005 she created Dance of Oneness®, her path of embodied spirituality. At UCLA she earned a Master of Fine Arts in dance and choreography and taught Persian dance. Her spiritual search took her to the Sufi tradition, the Gurdjieff Work and the Divine Feminine, while study of Chinese medicine, Tai Chi and Qigong gave her an understanding of the meridians and chakras that informs her movement work. She performs with her company, NAMAH, and with Andrew Harvey she made In the Fire of Grace, a dance film following Rumi's journey of the soul.

Dance of Oneness combines Sufi whirling, Persian dance, flamenco and contemporary movement with breath, meditation and wisdom teachings such as Rumi's poetry. She teaches both in person and online, giving workshops at centres including Esalen, Kripalu and Omega, and offers a library of video courses and a certification programme for future teachers. Her book Dance of Oneness: Embody Love and Luminosity to Transform Your Life, which has forewords by Anne Baring and Andrew Harvey, presents the method as a practical guide.
eluna-noelle:
Psychology, ancient wisdom, mythology, consciousness and intuitive practice all meet in the work of Eluña Noelle, a psycho-spiritual teacher who says she has had heightened intuitive awareness since early childhood. Starting college at sixteen, she took pre-medical courses at the University of Washington, then moved to The Evergreen State College to study psychology, human development and transpersonal psychology. Afterwards she gained a master's in Montessori education and became a certified Psychosynthesis life coach. She first read the Akashic Records privately for friends and clients; since her first public channelling, in January 2024, her online following has grown large.

Her teaching moves between study and direct experience, drawing on meditation, breathwork, guided writing, voice, contemplation and embodiment, and gives particular weight to the mystery traditions and the archetypes of ancient Egypt. She leads The Circle, an online membership with live teachings and monthly meditations, as well as a year-long Living Mystery School, and her self-paced courses include one on accessing the Akashic Records. She teaches retreats at the Art of Living Retreat Center and Omega Institute and guides sacred journeys in Egypt. In late 2026 she announced that she is stepping back from trance channelling to focus on teaching.
miranda-macpherson:
Born in Australia, Miranda Macpherson trained at the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts before moving to the United Kingdom. At 26, asked by her teacher Rabbi Joseph Gelberman, she established the OneSpirit Interfaith Foundation in London; over the following decade she trained and ordained more than six hundred interfaith ministers and spiritual counsellors there. After a period of practice in the cave of Sri Ramana Maharshi in south India, she settled in 2005 in the San Francisco Bay Area and now lives in San Rafael.

An interfaith minister and spiritual teacher, she offers a feminine approach to surrender and nondual realisation, built around a practice she calls Ego Relaxation. She draws on the Diamond Approach, A Course in Miracles and Sri Ramana Maharshi, combining meditation, self-inquiry, devotion and mantra with psychological integration. She leads the Living Grace Global Sangha, offers home retreats on Zoom and in-person retreats in California, Europe and the Bahamas, and teaches courses regularly on The Shift Network. Her books are The Way of Grace and Boundless Love (first published under the name Miranda Holden); she also created the Cultivating Grace card deck and has recorded two albums of mantra.
mary-sise:
Licensed in New York State as a clinical social worker, Mary Sise has more than 35 years of clinical experience, and for over twenty years she has worked with energy psychology, a family of methods that combines focused attention with tapping on acupressure points. She is a former president of ACEP, the Association for Comprehensive Energy Psychology, holds its diplomate in comprehensive energy psychology and has presented at its annual conference for many years. With Sheila Sidney Bender she co-wrote The Energy of Belief.

At the centre of her teaching is her own form of Emotional Freedom Techniques (EFT), combining tapping, breath, intention and eye movements, together with meditation, sound and chakra work, with the aim of releasing limiting beliefs and living in line with the soul's guidance. The Soul Weaving Process, her later work, explores how split-off parts of the self can return to wholeness, and she directs the Magdalena Healing programme. She teaches recorded courses on her own site and The Shift Network, runs free weekly tapping groups, and offers a monthly mentorship for coaches, therapists and healers.
stephen-dinan:
In 2010 Stephen Dinan founded The Shift Network, which he leads as chief executive, to bring spiritual teachers, thinkers and healers to a global audience through online courses, summits and trainings. He studied human biology at Stanford University and East-West psychology at CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies. Earlier in his career he co-created and directed the Center for Theory & Research at the Esalen Institute, and at the Institute of Noetic Sciences, where he directed membership and marketing, he led the Shift in Action programme and the One Minute Shift media series.

In his own teaching he joins spiritual practice with purpose, leadership and social change. His book Sacred America, Sacred World offers a hopeful, transpartisan vision of a nation and a world guided by spiritual values, and he edited Radical Spirit, an anthology of writing by a younger generation of spiritual voices. Among the gatherings where he has spoken are the World Cultural Forum in China and, in Costa Rica, the Alliance for a New Humanity. These days he mentors spirit-led teachers and entrepreneurs in reaching a wider audience with their work. He lives in San Rafael, California.
davina-mackail:
With more than 35 years of experience, Davina MacKail works as a shamanic teacher and feng shui consultant. Nursing was her first training. She took up shamanic practice in the 1990s and deepened it through the Pachakuti Mesa tradition of don Oscar Miro-Quesada and a long apprenticeship in New York with Alex Stark. She also qualified professionally in geomancy and feng shui, and for close to twenty years has taken pilgrimage groups to Peru with the Q'ero teacher Puma Fredy Quispe Singona. At London's College of Psychic Studies she was the first person to teach shamanism, and she co-founded the Ayni Foundation.

She sees the home as a living mirror of those who live in it, and her work combines classical feng shui and space clearing with astrology, tarot, the Gene Keys and shamanic ceremony. She offers consultations and mentoring online and in person, and every fortnight sends out a Moon Report, with a guided shamanic journey at each full moon. Her courses include an introduction to feng shui for Hay House and Shamanic Feng Shui on The Shift Network, and Hay House also publishes her books Feng Shui Made Easy and The Dream Whisperer.
laura-koniver:
Trained in conventional medicine, Dr. Laura Koniver is a physician who later moved to a holistic approach centred on grounding, the practice of being in direct physical contact with the Earth. Her book The Earth Prescription (Reveal Press, 2020) collects grounding practices for every season and has been translated into several languages. She has featured in documentaries on grounding, among them The Earthing Movie, Down to Earth, Heal for Free and The Grounded. She also paints and writes a regular column for MaryJanesFarm magazine.

She explains grounding in plain language: why the body's electrical connection with the ground matters to her, easy ways to ground indoors and outdoors through the seasons, and how to make the practice part of everyday life. As The Intuition Physician she shares hundreds of short teaching videos, guided grounding meditations and online classes on intuition and the chakras, and she runs small in-person grounding retreats in the eastern United States. She also offers free events and online courses on The Shift Network.
sue-frederick:
Based in Scottsdale, Arizona, Rev. Sue Frederick is an intuitive, numerologist and ordained Unity minister who has studied numerology since 1980. She also practises past-life and between-lives soul regression therapy, and describes herself as a channel for angelic guidance and for messages from loved ones who have died. Earlier she worked as a magazine editor and corporate vice president, led survival courses for Outward Bound, and taught at Naropa University and the University of Colorado. The early death of her husband, and what she calls three shared-death experiences, shaped her outlook.

In what she calls Sacred Numerology, the numbers in a birth date are read as a map of soul purpose, relationships and cycles of timing; she teaches this alongside angelic guidance, meditation and sacred writing. Her books include I See Your Dream Job, Bridges to Heaven, I See Your Soul Mate, Through a Divine Lens, Angels & Numbers and the Angel Up! series. She teaches live courses on Zoom and self-paced video classes, runs a group on Patreon, hosts the Mystical Conversations podcast and YouTube channel, and teaches on The Shift Network. She sits on the board of Helping Parents Heal as an honorary member.
maureen-hancock:
Maureen Hancock, a spirit medium, intuitive teacher and author, is based in the Bridgewater area of Massachusetts. She worked as a litigation manager before becoming a full-time medium, and for more than 25 years she has encouraged people to talk more openly about death, dying and grief. Her book is The Medium Next Door, and in 2011 the Style Network made her the subject of a documentary, Psychic in Suburbia. She volunteers with hospice, sits with bereaved parents, and has helped families and law enforcement with missing-person cases.

Intuition and spirit communication are the focus of her teaching: recognising signs from loved ones who have died, clearing what she calls the clutter that gets in the way of connection, and learning to test and trust intuitive impressions. Maureen Hancock University, her online school, offers self-paced semesters of lessons and meditations, and she gives workshops for medical professionals, law enforcement and the public. She tours New England with Postcards from Heaven, evenings of group readings, and leads Soul Shift retreats in Costa Rica and on Cape Cod that combine breathwork, meditation, intuitive exercises and mediumship. She founded The Zen Loft, a yoga and wellness centre in Bridgewater, and teaches on The Shift Network.
donna-lozito:
For several decades Donna Lozito, an interspecies animal communicator and nationally certified classical homeopath, has worked with people and their animal companions. After training at the School of Homeopathy in New York, she went on to study with Rajan Sankaran, Farokh Master and Frederik Schroyens in England and India. For the American College of Homeopathy, based in Phoenix, Arizona, she has also supervised and taken part in homeopathic provings. Her work with animals has taken her as far as Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Turkey and Israel, including work with camels.

She combines telepathic communication with animals, whether living or in spirit, with classical homeopathy and intuitive coaching, and puts the emphasis on compassion, listening and seeing through another being's eyes. Clients work with her by phone and Zoom; she also runs a mentorship programme for people building their own animal communication skills, and teaches online classes, live and recorded, on energy communication and the art of listening. Her children's story, Sweet Dreams: The Talking Horse from Brooklyn, is in print, and she has taught on The Shift Network, including within its animal communication certificate programme.
ibrahim-jaffe:
Dr. R. Ibrahim Jaffe, a physician, teaches in the Shadhiliyya Sufi tradition. After taking his medical degree at the University of Illinois he practised in Arizona, Hawaii and California, before turning his work fully to spiritual teaching. In 1996 Sidi Muhammad al-Jamal ar-Rifa'i, a Sufi master, accepted him as a student, and after years of training gave him authorisation (ijaza) to teach, with the title Murshid Murabbi Ruhi, a guide and caretaker of the soul.

In 2000 he founded the Jaffe Institute, which later became the Institute of Spiritual Healing and the University of Sufism, where he is founding Chancellor; through the Ma'rifa Foundation he co-leads the Shadhiliyya Ma'rifa community. He teaches Sufism as a path of divine love, centred on dhikr (remembrance of God), purification of the heart, the Divine Names and the heart's stations, along with APIIR-TB, a method of spiritual inquiry he developed. Online he offers Wisdom Wednesdays, a free weekly teaching series, as well as Friday Jumu'ah teachings and a monthly full moon dhikr. His book is God's Way: Sufi Spiritual Healing, and he is based in the Florida Keys.
lydia-de-leon:
Dr. Lydia de León, an architect and researcher from Greece, studies the ways in which buildings and places affect the people within them. She studied architecture at the National Technical University of Athens and took an MSc in Sustainable Environmental Design at London's Architectural Association, then completed a PhD in geobiology at the University of Ioannina, examining how geophysical anomalies affect living systems. For about fifteen years she has investigated why ancient temples stand where they do, measuring geometry, materials, earth fields and celestial alignments at sacred sites.

Geophilia, the design studio and school she co-founded with her partner, the architect Arturo Ponce de León, has bases in Greece, Mexico and Spain and brings building biology and sacred geometry into architecture. She developed the Healing Architecture approach, and her book The Power of Sacred Location grew out of her doctoral research. She teaches online courses on the sacred science of ancient temples, runs the Return to the Temple membership and leads temple retreats with Arturo, belongs to the faculty of Resonance Academy, and offers a live course on The Shift Network called Ancient Temple Codes.
neil-douglas-klotz:
Born in America and now living in Scotland, Neil Douglas-Klotz is a scholar, writer, musician and meditation teacher. His work concerns the spirituality of the native Middle East, and he translates from Hebrew, Aramaic and Arabic, above all the Aramaic words of Jesus. He has served as co-chair of the American Academy of Religion's Mysticism Group, directs the Edinburgh Institute for Advanced Learning, and in 1982 was a co-founder of the International Network for the Dances of Universal Peace. Under the name Saadi he is also a Sufi teacher in the lineage of Samuel L. Lewis.

Among his books are Revelations of the Aramaic Jesus, Original Meditation, Prayers of the Cosmos, The Hidden Gospel and The Aramaic Jesus Book of Days, as well as Desert Wisdom, The Little Book of Sufi Stories, The Sufi Book of Life, edited collections of Kahlil Gibran, and a novel. He teaches as much through chant, breath, meditation and sacred movement as through texts, leading online events and retreats through the Abwoon Network, and he has recorded four on-demand courses on the Aramaic Jesus for The Shift Network.
john-douillard:
Dr. John Douillard, a chiropractor and Ayurvedic practitioner, has been teaching Ayurveda for around forty years. He was once a professional athlete and later worked with the New Jersey Nets basketball team, overseeing player development as its director. His first book, Body, Mind, and Sport, described an approach to exercise based on ease, nasal breathing and body type. In Boulder, Colorado, he founded LifeSpa, which runs an Ayurvedic clinic and publishes his weekly videos and articles.

He brings classical Ayurvedic ideas together with modern research, teaching the doshas and emotional body types, routines for each day and season, pranayama and nasal breathing, abhyanga (Ayurvedic self-massage), yoga and meditation. Much of this he shares freely on YouTube and on his podcast, Ayurveda Meets Modern Science. He has written seven books, The Encyclopedia of Ayurvedic Massage among them, and teaches self-paced courses in Ayurveda on The Shift Network.
perdita-finn:
Perdita Finn writes and teaches about building a working relationship with the ancestors and the dead. Her teachers have included Zen teachers, priests, spirit workers and healers, and she served an apprenticeship with the psychic Suzan Saxman; together they wrote The Reluctant Psychic. She and her husband Clark Strand, a former Zen monk, co-founded The Way of the Rose, a lay rosary fellowship centred on the divine feminine and on what they describe as ecology, not theology; their book of the same name tells how it began.

Animism, ancestor veneration and older, mother-centred traditions run through her teaching and through her books Take Back the Magic: Conversations with the Unseen World and Mothers of Magic: Summoning the Wisdom of Our Ancestors. Working with altars, ritual, oracles, dreamwork and prayer, she teaches through Zoom workshops, a year-long course called A Year of Living with the Dead, monthly gatherings for readers of her Substack, and self-paced courses on The Shift Network. Her home is in the Catskill Mountains of New York.
christine-stevens:
Christine Stevens, a music therapist, author and drum circle facilitator, teaches drumming and the Native American-style flute as practices of spirituality and sound healing. She holds master's degrees in social work and music therapy and founded UpBeat Drum Circles. She has led drum circles for companies, communities, refugee women and survivors of disasters, among them the first drum circle peace training in northern Iraq. After singing Lakota prayer songs and taking part in Hanbleceya for more than ten years, Uncle Manny Eagle Elk Council Pipe Sandoval welcomed her by adoption into a Native American family. She also carries a pipe for Women's Way Long Dance.

She plays hand drums, frame drums, crystal bowls, flute and voice, often outdoors at sacred natural sites, and stresses improvisation, ceremony and reciprocity with nature. Her offerings include online courses and trainings, the Global Rhythm Sangha each month, and a series of self-paced drumming and flute courses on The Shift Network. Among her books are The Healing Drum Kit, Music Medicine, The Nature Sutras and The Art and Heart of Drum Circles. She lives in Encinitas, California.
raja-choudhury:
Raja Choudhury, whom his students call Rajada, teaches Kundalini Shakti, Tantra and Kriya Yoga and makes documentary films. After training as an architect at the Architectural Association in London, he worked in London and New York as a digital creative director, and in 2006 a Kundalini awakening turned his life in a new direction. Moving to India, he made films about spiritual teachers and wisdom traditions, among them one on his teacher, Guruji Amritananda, and Spirituality in the Modern World, featuring Ken Wilber. The Quantum Indians received India's National Film Award in 2014, PBS broadcast America's First Guru, about Swami Vivekananda, and in 2012 he gave a TED talk on Indian wisdom.

His teaching draws on Shaiva and Shakta Tantra, Sri Vidya, the Vigyan Bhairav Tantra and Vedanta, set beside modern psychology and neuroscience, with breath, mantra and meditation at the core, and he encourages students to be their own guru. He teaches online on The Shift Network and runs A Thousand Suns Academy, which offers a monthly membership, The Path, along with on-demand programmes. His lengthy talks on Shiva, Kundalini and the third eye draw large audiences on YouTube. He lives in Princeton, New Jersey.
tina-zion:
Based in Indianapolis, Indiana, Tina Zion is an author, teacher and intuitive medium who describes herself as a fourth-generation intuitive. For many years she was a registered nurse, certified as a specialist in mental health nursing. She trained as a Gestalt counsellor at the Indianapolis Gestalt Institute and holds a degree in communication and management. She is certified in clinical hypnotherapy, focusing on past-life regression, and trained in Life Between Lives regression with the Michael Newton Institute. Having reached the level of Reiki Master-Teacher, she taught Reiki for over ten years.

Her teaching centres on mediumship and developing intuition, including how a medium can work with spirit guides and help the deceased move on. She teaches in person and online; her courses have taken her to Canada, Mexico, Australia, New Zealand, Europe and the United Kingdom, and in the United States to Omega Institute and Fellowships of the Spirit. Her books include Reiki and Your Intuition, The Reiki Teacher's Manual, and Healing Ghosts, Haunted Places, and Non-Human Beings, a training manual for mediums. Recorded courses are also available through her own website and The Shift Network.
william-bloom:
Meditation, subtle energy and modern spirituality are the fields in which Dr. William Bloom, a British author and teacher born in London in 1948, has spent his working life. Early on he wrote novels and worked as a commissioning editor at Macmillan, then lived for two years on an off-grid retreat in Morocco's High Atlas Mountains, an experience recorded in The Sacred Magician. A doctorate in political psychology followed at the LSE, where he taught as well, and he went on to spend a decade teaching adults and teenagers with special needs. At St James's Church, Piccadilly, he co-founded the Alternatives programme; he has taught at the Findhorn Foundation for many years and served at length as a Glastonbury Abbey trustee.

The Spiritual Companions Trust, an educational charity he founded and still leads, created the first vocational qualification in spirituality registered with Ofqual, and today it brings spiritual wellbeing into schools. His approach is practical and gathers from many traditions: a daily meditation practice, work with subtle energy, psychic protection, and a calm, unafraid attitude to death and dying. Translated into sixteen languages, his books include Psychic Protection, The Endorphin Effect, Working With Angels, Fairies and Nature Spirits and a title on the new spirituality. Online, he teaches through The Shift Network and Watkins Wisdom Academy.
rob-schwartz:
Rob (Robert) Schwartz, an American author and hypnotist, focuses on pre-birth planning: the view that, as souls, we plan our lives before we are born, our hardest challenges included. Until 2003 he worked in the corporate world; that year a session with a medium turned his life in a new direction. Over the following years he worked with mediums and channels to explore the pre-birth plans of many people, and the result was three books on the theme. Your Soul's Plan was followed by Your Soul's Gift and then Your Soul's Love, and together they have appeared in more than twenty-five languages.

Between Lives Soul Regression has been part of his work since 2012: a form of hypnosis in which a person revisits a past life, then speaks with a council of wise, loving guides about the plan for their present life. He makes clear that he is not himself a medium or a channel. Venues where he has taught include Kripalu, 1440 Multiversity and Hollyhock, and he also teaches online through The Shift Network. His wife, Liesel Fricke, channels a group they call the Beings of Light; together they lead online group regressions and Rise to the Path, a monthly membership and mentoring community.
richard-tarnas:
A cultural historian and philosopher, Richard Tarnas draws together the history of ideas, depth psychology and archetypal astrology. At CIIS in San Francisco (the California Institute of Integral Studies) he founded the Philosophy, Cosmology, and Consciousness programme and taught there for some thirty years, on the evolution of consciousness, Jungian and archetypal psychology and archetypal cosmology; he is now Professor Emeritus. Earlier, he spent ten years at Esalen Institute in Big Sur, rising to director of programmes and education, and he has been a regular lecturer at Pacifica Graduate Institute.

The Passion of the Western Mind, widely used in universities, follows Western thought from ancient Greece into the postmodern era. In Cosmos and Psyche: Intimations of a New World View he argues for correlations between planetary cycles and archetypal patterns, both in history and in individual lives; the Scientific and Medical Network named it its Book of the Year. Prometheus the Awakener, a shorter essay, looks at the archetype of Uranus. He was once president of the International Transpersonal Association. These days he teaches mostly online, with courses at the Kosmos Institute and, alongside Stanislav Grof, the Psyche & Cosmos programmes on The Shift Network.
david-gandelman:
With a light and often humorous touch, meditation teacher and author David Gandelman teaches meditation, energy awareness and intuitive development. After studying Western philosophy at Rutgers University, he lived in the Himalayas, where he studied the spiritual traditions of the East, and later became director of a Hawaiian school devoted to mysticism and intuitive development. Cornell University has hosted his meditation teaching, as have organisations such as NBC Universal and SAP, and many people use his guided meditations on the Insight Timer app.

Meditation School, which he founded, is an online membership and app offering courses and daily meditations. He hosts three podcasts: Meditation School, Energy Matters and Grounded Sleep. Together with Cody Edner he runs the Energy Matters Academy, whose courses cover seeing and reading energy, the intuitive chakras and kundalini, alongside in-person retreats; with Michael Galyon he leads a meditation teacher training lasting a year. In The 7 Energies of the Soul he describes seven archetypal energies (creator, healer, warrior, lover, artist, explorer and master), offering exercises and meditations for balancing them. His course on The Shift Network, Third Eye Training, covers intuition and energy reading.
joan-ranquet:
For around thirty years Joan Ranquet, an American animal communicator, energy worker and teacher, has worked professionally with animals and the people who live with them. In her view animal communication is a skill anyone can learn rather than a rare gift. Her teaching covers telepathic connection with animals, grounding, sensing the energy of a home, the chakras of dogs, cats and horses, EFT tapping for animals and their guardians, and staying connected with animals after they die. Home is a small ranch in southern California, where her horses, dogs and cats also act as teaching partners for her students.

CWALU, short for Communication With All Life University, is the school she founded in 2009; it offers courses and certification online and in person in animal communication, energy work, and nature and wildlife. Among her books are Communication With All Life (Hay House), Energy Healing for Animals (Sounds True), Animal Chakra Healing (Findhorn Press), and a book on EFT for animals and their people co-written with Ellie Laks. She has given a TEDx talk about animals in transition, takes groups on wildlife journeys to places such as Thula Thula in South Africa, and offers self-paced courses on The Shift Network.
marion-gilbert:
Marion Gilbert, an American teacher of embodied awareness, founded the Somatic Enneagram. She has been a registered physical therapist since 1978, and in Grass Valley, California, she runs her own practice and a movement studio; she also trained in craniosacral therapy and SomatoEmotional Release. Her work with the Enneagram began in 2003. Four years later she joined the core faculty of the Narrative Enneagram tradition, and she is still adjunct faculty of The Narrative Enneagram. She is also on the advisory board of the Enneagram Prison Project.

In her hands the Enneagram becomes a map of the body as much as of thought and feeling. Students learn to notice how their type appears in physical habits and reactions, through three practices: grounded presence, cultivating an inner observer and placing attention deliberately. The aim is to bring body, heart and mind into balance, a state she calls three-centred awareness. She teaches the Somatic Enneagram through online training modules, a professional certification path and residential retreats in the United States, Europe and Egypt. A free weekly online meditation is part of her offering, she appears on The Somatic Enneagram Podcast, and a new programme with The Shift Network is in preparation.
silvia-nakkach:
Silvia Nakkach, whose spiritual name is Saraswati Devi, is a musician, composer and vocalist with a Grammy nomination to her name. She trained and worked as a music psychotherapist before turning to the voice as a spiritual practice. For around four decades she has studied North Indian classical singing, above all the Dhrupad style of raga. At CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies in San Francisco, she taught for more than sixteen years and designed a certificate programme in sound, voice and music for the healing arts.

The Vox Mundi Project, which she founded, is an international school of sound and the voice based in the San Francisco Bay Area and in Brazil. Her method, The Yoga of the Voice, combines deep listening, breath, chanting, raga, improvisation and shamanic medicine melodies, and she teaches it through modular certificate trainings, retreats and online courses, among them programmes on The Shift Network. She has released many albums of devotional and ambient music. Free Your Voice, a book written with Valerie Carpenter, gathers more than a hundred vocal exercises for people without musical training.
marguerite-mary-rigoglioso:
Marguerite Mary Rigoglioso studies the religions of the ancient Mediterranean and teaches the Sacred Feminine; she is best known for research on traditions of divine and virgin birth and on Mother Mary and Mary Magdalene. From CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies, she holds a PhD in Humanities and an MA in Philosophy and Religion. She trained in intuitive development with the Foundation for Spiritual Development and taught religion and women's spirituality at several Bay Area universities. Later, at Canterbury Christ Church University in England, she helped set up a master's programme on myth, cosmology and the sacred.

Seven Sisters Mystery School, founded in 2012, is where she teaches the oracle and priestess traditions of the ancient world, the lineage of the Marys, the Pleiades and the faery realms. She pairs historical scholarship with guided meditation, ceremony and oracular transmission, offered as on-demand courses, a monthly online membership called the Inner Sanctum Temple, and a Mary and Magdalene priestess training over six months. Her books include a study of the secret life of Mother Mary, a book on the mystery tradition of miraculous conception, and two academic works, one on the ancient Greek cult of divine birth and one on the virgin mother goddesses of antiquity.
viviane-chauvet:
Viviane Chauvet channels and teaches what she presents as Arcturian wisdom, calling herself an ambassador for the Arcturians, a star nation she says she works with directly. Her training spans several energy-healing and intuitive methods: certifications with the ThetaHealing Institute and the HeartMath Institute, in Dolores Cannon's QHHT and in the Unity Field Technique, along with study of Reiki and meditation. For more than fifteen years she has taught and spoken internationally, and she created two systems of her own, Arcturian Energy Matrix Healing and an Arcturian healing arts programme.

At the Arcturian University, the online school she founded, she gives a two-hour master class each month and leads group meditations and community gatherings, with a free library of meditations and introductory talks alongside. Her retreats take place at sacred sites in Sedona, Nepal, Germany and New Zealand among others, and she has taught on The Shift Network. She shares long guided meditations, such as the Rays of Creation series, without charge on YouTube, and her own story is told in the documentary An Arcturian Experience. She co-hosts the Infinite Star Connections podcast and has written chapters for several anthologies, The Way of the Initiate among them.
gemma-petherbridge:
Gemma Petherbridge, a British crystal healer, Akashic Records reader and teacher, grew up near Stonehenge and Avebury and says she has been psychic since childhood. When she lost both parents in her early twenties, she left a corporate career behind for spiritual study, and across more than twenty years she has built up a wide range of qualifications in crystal healing, energy work and related fields. Conscience Crystals came first, in 2017; she then founded The Crystal Mystery School, an online academy running accredited trainings.

Courses at the school include crystal healing certification, Akashic Records reading at two levels (first personal practice, then professional practitioner training) and cacao ceremony facilitation, delivered through live online classes, recorded lessons and a student community. In London she teaches workshops on intuition, meditation writing and crystal lore for the College of Psychic Studies, and she also teaches on The Shift Network. Octopus publishes her books: Your Crystal Plan; The Crystal Almanac, which follows crystals through the seasons, lunar phases and festivals of the year; and Find Your Light, a guide to lightwork and intuition.
lisa-rafel:
Before she became a spiritual teacher and sound healer, Lisa Rafel worked as an actress, playwright, songwriter and producer. The American teacher is known for Vocal Sound Healing™, which uses the voice, chant and overtones for self-healing and in work with others, and she has taught vocal sound for more than thirty years. Guided meditation, prayer, energy exercises and psychic "seeing" all feature in her classes, shaped by Kabbalah and by Tibetan, Mongolian, ancient Egyptian and Native American practices. She has sung at Chartres Cathedral, the Great Pyramid and Tibet's Sakya Monastery.

Her live online teaching happens in small groups. The Five Worlds is a two-day programme passing through five thresholds towards a more integrated sense of self; alongside it run Psychic Wisdom, Vocal Sound Healing classes and small ongoing groups she calls pods. She is on the faculty of The Shift Network and the Globe Sound Healing Institute, and also teaches at Rancho La Puerta in Mexico. Lisa's World, her low-cost membership, holds a library of her meditations, prayers and talks. Through her company Resonant Sounds, and with Gary Malkin and her husband David Surrenda, she co-created Safe in the Arms of Love, a book and music set on parent and baby bonding.
anamika-neitlich:
Anamika Neitlich, known in her writing and teaching simply as Anamika, is an American teacher of consciousness and energy work living in California. After studying psychology at Wellesley College, she took a PhD in psychology at Columbia Pacific University, and she also graduated from the Barbara Brennan School of Healing. She says she has perceived energy since early childhood. Over five decades of private sessions, groups and workshops with people around the world, her work has come to combine psychology, metaphysics, spirituality and energy healing.

She describes her approach as invitational rather than instructional. Her sessions and gatherings centre on presence, deep listening and what she calls coherence transmissions: guided energetic journeys intended to help people experience more of who they are. She sees individuals and couples by Zoom or phone, leads small shared intensive groups and a community membership, and gives a monthly online workshop with a new theme each time; sessions are also offered in French. Among her books are and…, Loving Now, Love in Fur Coats, about her animal companions, and French Lessons in Love. She also teaches on The Shift Network.
cassandra-vieten:
Spirituality, transformative experiences, mindfulness and the science of imagination are the research interests of clinical psychologist Cassandra Vieten. Her PhD in clinical psychology comes from CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies, and she trained in behavioural genetics research at the University of California, San Francisco. For many years she worked at the Institute of Noetic Sciences, serving as President from 2013 to 2019 and remains a Senior Fellow, and she later led the John W. Brick Mental Health Foundation. At UC San Diego she is a Clinical Professor and directs the Center for Mindfulness.

She brings research and practice together in her teaching. Through workshops at places such as Esalen, as well as talks and online courses, she explores how people change, how imagination shapes our thoughts, feelings and actions, and how meditation and contemplative practice can become part of everyday life. Imagine That looks at the science of imagination; Living Deeply, written with Marilyn Schlitz and Tina Amorok, studies transformation across traditions; and Spiritual and Religious Competencies in Clinical Practice, with Shelley Scammell, sets out guidelines for therapists. She teaches on The Shift Network as well.
linda-star-wolf:
Shamanic Breathwork, the ceremonial practice created by shamanic teacher Linda Star Wolf, combines cyclical breathing, chakra-attuned music, bodywork, art and group sharing. In the 1970s she started out as a therapist and counsellor, and she studied breathwork and consciousness with teachers including Ram Dass, Leonard Orr, Stanislav Grof and Jacquelyn Small. During the 1990s she trained with the Eupsychia Institute and studied the Wolf Clan teachings of Twylah Nitsch, a Seneca elder who adopted her as a spiritual granddaughter and gave her the name Star Wolf.

On Dove Mountain in North Carolina she founded the Venus Rising Association for Transformation and Venus Rising University. There, students follow a training path she calls S.H.I.P., an initiatory shamanic process, to become Shamanic Breathwork facilitators and shamanic ministers. She and her husband, Nikólaus Wolf, lead Shamanic Mystery Tours to sacred sites in Egypt, Peru, Bali and elsewhere, and host small retreats in Portugal. Thirteen books carry her name as author or co-author, including Shamanic Breathwork, Visionary Shamanism, Shamanic Mysteries of Egypt with Nicki Scully, and The Aquarian Shaman, which is also the name of the broadcast she hosts. She teaches on The Shift Network.
alex-dong:
Alex Dong is a fourth-generation master of the Dong (Tung) family style of Taijiquan, the lineage founded by his great-grandfather Dong Yingjie. His formal training started at five in Hebei Province under his father, Grand Master Dong Zeng Chen. The family moved to Honolulu when he was twelve, and there his grandfather, Grand Master Dong Hu Ling, became his teacher too. By fifteen he was assisting in his father's classes; he opened his own class in Hawaii in 1990, and in 1991 took the US national title in moving push hands. After moving to New York City in 2003, he founded the Alex Dong International Taijiquan Association.

He teaches the family's slow, fast, Fa-Jing and Kai-He (Hao) forms, push hands, weapons and foundational qigong, as well as shorter Simplified and Advanced forms of his own design. Weekly classes run in New York, with live and recorded lessons online and seminars across the United States, Europe and Asia; his instructional videos are sold through his own site. He also founded an organisation to carry on Tung Ying Jie's legacy, translated much of his great-grandfather's Taijiquan Explained (the Red Book), and, with David Saltman, co-wrote Grand Master, a biography of Dong Yingjie.
simcha-raphael:
Simcha Paull Raphael, a rabbi, psychotherapist and teacher, has devoted his life's work to bringing together Jewish tradition, psychology and the study of death and the afterlife. He was born in Quebec and studied at Concordia University in Montreal. In 1986 he received a PhD in psychology from CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies, and in 1990 Rabbi Zalman Schachter-Shalomi ordained him as a Rabbinic Chaplain. He has taught at Temple University, La Salle University and Bryn Athyn College and served as a spiritual director at the Reconstructionist Rabbinical College. In the Philadelphia area he works as a transpersonal psychotherapist, bereavement counsellor and spiritual director.

As founding director of the DA'AT Institute, which focuses on death awareness, advocacy and training, he gives lectures, scholar-in-residence weekends and professional trainings for clergy, hospice staff and caregivers. The topics include Jewish views of the afterlife, Kabbalah, death rituals and mourning. Jewish Views of the Afterlife, his best-known book, is now in a third edition. Later titles include The Grief Journey and the Afterlife, May the Angels Carry You, Living and Dying in Ancient Times and Spirits, Ghosts, & Dybbuks, and he has also published collections of poetry.
lauren-rainbow:
Lauren Rainbow is an evidential medium, spiritual teacher and sacred travel guide living in New Hampshire. In 2001 a run of synchronicities opened her to sensing and hearing loved ones in spirit, and from there she trained with a number of established mediums. Having grown up in community theatre, she feels most at home demonstrating on stage. She has worked alongside mediums such as Tony Stockwell and John Holland, and with Holland she co-wrote The Mediumship Training Deck for Hay House. Omega Institute, Kripalu and Lily Dale have all hosted her teaching.

Evidential mediumship and Akashic Soul Sessions sit at the heart of her work, together with teaching on intuition, spirit guides and heart-centred meditation. In New England she gives private sessions, live evenings of spirit messages, and meditation and sound bath events; online she runs a community with monthly practice circles and sells guided meditations and Akashic Records courses. Since 2017 she has taken small groups on sacred journeys to Egypt, India, Peru, Nepal and Mexico. Her guided meditations can also be found on Hay House Unlimited and on her YouTube channel.
maria-furlano:
Maria Furlano, an American Qigong teacher and energy intuitive, is based in Southern California. Her path began at twelve with Taekwon-Do, in which she earned a second-degree black belt. She later trained in bodywork, completed a master's degree in Traditional Oriental Medicine at Emperor's College in Los Angeles, and became a licensed acupuncturist in California. In Beijing she studied Qigong with Master Wan Sujian, and she completed doctoral-level Qigong training with the International Institute of Medical Qigong under Bernard Shannon, later teaching there herself.

The Art Of Tuning In, the online studio she founded, is where she teaches breath, movement and meditation as ways to sense and steady one's own energy. She gives particular attention to sensitive people and to anyone whose work involves holding space for others. Grounding, energetic boundaries, intuition and seasonal practice rooted in Chinese tradition are among her themes, taught through live classes, guided audio and private coaching. She has hosted The Art Of Tuning In Podcast since 2019 and posts short Qigong routines and guided meditations on her YouTube channel. She also teaches on The Shift Network.
judy-ramsey:
Working from her farm near Ann Arbor, Michigan, under the name Heart to Heart, Judy Liu Ramsey is an animal communicator, shamanic practitioner and ordained animal chaplain. She holds an MA from the University of Michigan and was a social work counsellor and craniosacral therapist before she turned to animal communication nearly twenty years ago. Penelope Smith trained her in telepathic animal communication and Teresa Wagner in grief and hospice communication. Her shamanic practice developed through mentoring with Sandra Ingerman and others, with further study under Tom Cowan, Alberto Villoldo and Betsy Bergstrom, and in 2023 she was ordained through the Compassion Consortium.

Her animal communication teaching runs across four levels, from basic telepathic communication up to interspecies counselling. Sandra Ingerman has approved her to teach Ingerman's own courses, among them Basic Journeying, Healing with Spiritual Light and Medicine for the Earth, along with advanced practitioner trainings. Most of her classes are live on Zoom; she also holds an online journey circle twice a month, gives private sessions for people and their animals, and leads small-group cultural journeys to Peru. She is practical and grounded, encouraging students to grow still and let the animals teach them. On YouTube she shares guided shamanic journeys and drumming for journeying.
cynthia-abulafia:
Cynthia Abulafia, a writer, educator and yoga therapist living in Santa Barbara, California, was initiated in a Shākta Tantra lineage of the Goddess. She studied in Naropa University's master's programme in yogic studies. For around twenty years she has explored different forms of non-duality alongside the scriptures of yoga and tantra, and for many years she designed and led yoga teacher trainings, among them as a lead trainer at Yoga Soup in Santa Barbara.

At the centre of her teaching are the divine feminine and what she calls the "transcendence bias": spiritual paths that show people how to rise above the body but not how to come back to it. Drawing on her own kundalini awakening, she supports people going through spiritual emergence with grounded practices of breath, the body, chanting and close reading of sacred texts. Monkfish published her first book, Embodying the Goddess, in 2026. She runs in-person workshops in California, a streamed course on the history and texts of yoga and Goddess tantra, a free book-club course and short talks on YouTube, and she writes on Substack.
lisa-wilcoxson:
Lisa Wilcoxson, an evidential medium and psychic, is based in Arizona. She says she first saw people in spirit as a teenager, though her mediumship only opened fully after both her children died: first her son Michael, who had complex special needs and never walked or spoke, and later her son Anthony. She has worked as a medium ever since and has passed the double-blind testing and certification of Find A Certified Medium. She is also a spiritual and grief coach and mentor.

Bereaved parents make up much of her work. For Helping Parents Heal she is a recommended provider and honorary board member, and she leads two of its affiliate groups: one for parents whose children with special needs have died, and one for parents whose only child, or every child, has died. She gives individual mediumship and psychic readings online by Zoom, as well as group readings, and talks about grief and the afterlife at events and on podcasts. She contributed to the anthology Gathering at the Doorway. With her husband, Rick, she lives in Scottsdale and Sedona.
kate-belew:
Poet, author and teacher Kate Belew brings creative writing together with witchcraft and folk magic. She grew up in Michigan and studied English at Kalamazoo College, then took an MFA in poetry at Sarah Lawrence. Her training in green witchcraft came through a three-year apprenticeship with Robin Rose Bennett; she also studied herbalism at the Chestnut School of Herbs and astrology with Rebecca Gordon, and she is an initiated Green Witch. She lives in Brooklyn.

Since 2017 she has led writing circles and workshops both in person and online. The Bardo, her five-week programme, gathers writers for sessions on ritual, storytelling and channelled and automatic writing. On Substack, her Word Witch newsletter carries weekly essays and seven-line writing prompts, and paying members can join live writing circles. Word Witch (2025), her book, shows how to build a writing practice through simple rituals. With Shelby Bundy of Tamed Wild, where she co-hosted the Magick & Alchemy podcast, she co-wrote Wild Medicine, an illustrated guide to the folklore and magic of more than sixty herbs. Her poems and essays have been published in a range of journals and magazines.
helen-hamilton:
An English spiritual teacher, Helen Hamilton teaches in the non-dual tradition of Self-realisation. Her teaching arose from her own awakening, which she experienced as a long and difficult process, and she wants to make that path simpler and available to anyone. As she puts it, the truth of who we are is simple, and anyone can realise the Self. She was based in West Yorkshire for many years and is a mother of four.

Satsang is her main form: a talk followed by open questions, offered free on Zoom twice a month. Alongside these she holds weekend intensives and residential retreats in Britain, Spain and the United States, many of them recorded. Five practices underpin her method: meditation, contemplation, self-inquiry, conscious imagining and what she calls the Statement Process. Those who want to go deeper can join the Helen Hamilton Sangha, a monthly membership with live classes, a growing archive and support from acharya teachers she has trained. Balboa Press publishes her series of books, the first being Dissolving the Ego and Transcending the Mind, and several short ebooks are free on her website.
becca-tarnas:
Archetypal cosmology, depth psychology and the imagination are the fields of scholar and teacher Becca Tarnas. Raised in Big Sur, California, she attended the San Francisco Waldorf School and then Mount Holyoke College, where she studied environmental studies and theatre. At CIIS, the California Institute of Integral Studies, she took a master's degree in Philosophy, Cosmology and Consciousness and a PhD in Ecology, Spirituality and Religion. Her dissertation, The Back of Beyond, set the 'Red Books' of Jung and Tolkien side by side as two journeys into the imaginal realm. She now teaches in the CIIS Philosophy, Cosmology and Consciousness programme as an Assistant Professor.

Her graduate courses cover Jung, archetypal astrology and Stanislav Grof's research, and she lectures widely, mostly online, for Jung societies and institutes on the Red Books, synchronicity and archetypal astrology. She is one of the editors of Archai, a journal of archetypal cosmology, and wrote Journey to the Imaginal Realm, a guide for readers of The Lord of the Rings. She narrated the audiobooks of Grof's The Way of the Psychonaut and When the Impossible Happens, and is now writing his biography. She and her family live in California, in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada.
matthew-fox:
Theologian and Episcopal priest Matthew Fox is best known for reviving Creation Spirituality, an earth-honouring mystical tradition that draws on the Western mystics, Indigenous wisdom, the arts and modern science. He was a Dominican for 34 years, and in Paris, at the Institut Catholique, he earned a doctorate in the history and theology of spirituality. The Institute in Culture and Creation Spirituality, which he founded, ran first at Mundelein College in Chicago and then at Holy Names University in Oakland; he went on to found the University of Creation Spirituality and served as its president until 2005.

Original Blessing, Creativity, The Coming of the Cosmic Christ and A Spirituality Named Compassion are among his more than 40 books. He has done much to return mystics such as Meister Eckhart, Hildegard of Bingen, Thomas Aquinas and Julian of Norwich to wider reading. The Four Paths of Creation Spirituality give his teaching its shape: awe, letting go, creativity and transformation. He offers recorded and live online courses, several with the cosmologist Brian Thomas Swimme or the writer Mirabai Starr, and the free Daily Meditations with Matthew Fox are written in his tradition.
jennifer-lisa-vest:
Known as "the Ethical Psychic", Dr. Jennifer Lisa Vest is an intuitive, Akashic records reader, medium and ceremonialist of Afro-Indigenous heritage, based in Berkeley, California. Her PhD, in Indigenous philosophy, is from the University of California, Berkeley; she also holds a history MA from Howard University and a physics BA from Hampshire College. She taught philosophy at two universities before turning to spiritual teaching full time. Her ceremonial training spans Native American sweat lodge, Hoodoo from the African American tradition, Caribbean spiritual healing and Spiritualism. She is a firekeeper, a Usui Reiki Master and a certified QHHT past-life regression practitioner.

Metatron's Academy of Spirit and Science, the online school she founded, offers self-paced courses on auras, the Akashic records and psychic development, and she teaches regularly on The Shift Network. In The Ethical Psychic she gives beginners a guide to working with intuitive gifts with integrity, while Sovereign Wisdom, from her academic career, proposes ways of building Native American philosophy from Indigenous cultures. Her YouTube talks cover spirit guides, ancestors, mediumship and the Akashic records, alongside psychic commentary on current events.
the-brothers-koren:
The Brothers Koren are Isaac and Thorald Koren, Australian-born brothers who moved to New York with their mother. For around fifteen years they performed as the band The Kin, earning a gold record and supporting acts including Coldplay, Bon Jovi, P!NK and Rod Stewart. In 2015 they left touring behind to teach, and created The Songwriter's Journey, a small-group programme that guides people with no musical background from a first idea all the way to a finished, recorded song of their own.

They approach the voice as an instrument of the whole body, and singing as a way back to presence, self-expression and belonging. Toning, breath, group singing, improvisation and songwriting are their tools, with the emphasis on play and on being heard rather than on technique. As well as their own online programmes and the Embodied Voice Portal membership, they run weekend workshops at Esalen, a free monthly online gathering called The Choir, and several courses on The Shift Network. They have given a TEDx talk and co-created The Journey, a documentary about the voice.
gary-kraftsow:
For more than forty years Gary Kraftsow, an American yoga teacher, has taught in the Viniyoga tradition. In 1974 he began studying with T.K.V. Desikachar in India, and in 1988, in Paris, he received a Viniyoga Special Diploma. He also holds a master's in psychology and religion from UC Santa Barbara. In the early 1980s he opened a school of yoga therapy on Maui, and he still directs the American Viniyoga Institute, which he set up in 1999. He helped to design the yoga protocols for two research studies run by the National Institutes of Health and for a trial of workplace stress reduction.

In his teaching, breath-centred āsana is joined with prāṇāyāma, chanting, mantra and meditation, all adapted to the individual, together with the philosophy of the Yoga Sūtras, Sāṁkhya and Tantra. At the institute he leads the Viniyoga Foundations Program and therapist training, and he also offers an online library of live and recorded classes, plus workshops and retreats in the US and abroad. Penguin is the publisher of both Yoga for Transformation and Yoga for Wellness, his two books, and he teaches several self-paced courses on The Shift Network.
lindsey-wei:
Shifu Lindsey Wei (Daoist name Wei Cheng Ling) is an American teacher of Wudang internal martial arts. She is a lay disciple of Wudang Daoism's Chun Yang sect, in its 24th generation. For more than nine years she trained under Master Li Xing De at the Five Immortals Temple on White Horse Mountain in China, studying Qigong, Tai Ji Quan, Ba Gua, the double-edged straight sword and Daoist meditation and scripture. She returned to the United States to teach in 2010. Those years are the subject of her memoir, The Valley Spirit: A Female Story of Daoist Cultivation.

At her school, Wudang White Horse, she teaches the temple curriculum as a single path of cultivation: stillness meditation, Yang Sheng Gong, Tai Ji, Ba Gua circle walking, kung fu basics and the Seven Star Sword. Students can join a monthly online membership with recorded courses and weekly live classes, or attend residential immersion camps held outdoors in southern Oregon's Siskiyou mountains, where training follows the rhythms of nature. The school says its aim is to teach students to teach themselves, so the practices become part of daily life. On The Shift Network she also offers self-paced courses in Wudang Qigong and Daoist meditation.
barry-goldstein:
Barry Goldstein, an American composer, producer and teacher, has worked with music, sound and vibration for more than thirty years. With Les Paul he co-produced "69 Freedom Special", a track that won a Grammy. He has composed for film, television and PBS specials, and created ambient soundscapes for authors and teachers including Dr. Joe Dispenza, Gregg Braden, Anita Moorjani, Neale Donald Walsch and Shirley MacLaine. Several of his albums have made the top ten of the Billboard New Age chart.

Beyond his own music, he teaches people to use sound with intention in daily life: heart-coherence breathing, toning and chanting, tuning forks, drumming, intention, and personal playlists for relaxation, focus and creativity. The Secret Language of the Heart, his book, with a foreword by Dr. Joe Dispenza, lays out these tools, among them the Heart Song breathing process. He teaches through online programmes on his Sound of Transformation portal, live online sound sessions and workshops, and self-paced courses on The Shift Network. Through Sonic Signatures he also creates sound identities for organisations.
renee-baribeau:
Renee Baribeau, an American shamanic practitioner, author and teacher who goes by The Practical Shaman, has around three decades of practice behind her. She has drawn on Q'ero, Lakota, Mapuche and other Andean teachings, and since 2010 has taught WindWork, her own system, at festivals such as Bhakti Fest and Shakti Fest, at Omega and online. In WindWork the winds serve as a compass for times of change. Students learn to read four primary winds and the gates that lie between them, and to bring ceremony, journeying and simple rituals such as wind knots and prayer flags into everyday life.

Winds of Spirit, her book with Hay House, won a Nautilus Gold award. Since then she has published A Pilgrim's Guide to Walking Wisdom and the Wind Walker's Wisdom Oracle, a deck of 64 cards, and Destiny Books is due to publish The Practical Shaman in 2027. On windwork.org she offers on-demand courses and monthly online journey circles; she also leads walking pilgrimages and teaches two WindWork courses on The Shift Network. With Sandra Ingerman she co-hosts The Shaman's Cave podcast, and she has her own podcast, The Practical Shaman.
melissa-kim-corter:
The shadow side of the psyche is the focus for depth psychologist and writer Melissa Kim Corter. At Pacifica Graduate Institute she earned both a master's degree and a doctorate in depth psychology, specialising in Jungian and archetypal studies; her doctoral thesis looked at psychopathy and the Western shadow. She also trained as a hypnotherapist at the Southwest Institute of Healing Arts. She is an ordained minister and a certified medicolegal death investigator, and serves on the board of the International Association for Jungian Studies.

In her teaching, fairy tales, myth, film, dreams and journaling become ways to meet the hidden and disowned parts of ourselves instead of turning away from them. Her self-paced programmes cover Jungian shadow work, soulful writing and the dark feminine; she gives private consultations to writers and creatives, and writes The Shadow Psychologist on Substack. Among her books are Apothecary for the Afflicted, a collection of shadow work practices, Esoterica: The Shadow Worker's Codex, and the Wild Woman's book series. Her courses on The Shift Network explore the myths of the dark goddess and the alchemy of fairy tales.
rebecca-dawson:
Rebecca Dawson is an Australian channel, author and teacher who has worked with channelled material for more than thirty years. She began speaking as a channel at the age of eighteen, and her teachings are presented as coming from a group she calls the Masters, among them Serapis Bey, St Germain and Kuthumi. Her themes include the shift in human consciousness, the nature of time and dimensional reality, purpose and conscious creation.

Her books are The Game of Purpose, The Agreement and The New Human Experience, along with a fourth called Fu: The Return of the Magnetic Human. She teaches mainly online through livestream series, recorded seminars with transcripts, a monthly membership with live question-and-answer sessions and wisdom circles, and occasional in-person retreats and expo appearances. She also offers private channelled sessions over Zoom, has contributed articles to the Sedona Journal of Emergence, and has been a guest on many podcasts. In 2026 she taught a seven-week live course on perception on The Shift Network.
yuval-ron:
Yuval Ron is an Israeli-born composer, oud player and teacher of sacred music, based in Los Angeles. He leads the Yuval Ron Ensemble, which brings together Jewish, Sufi, Christian and Armenian musical traditions, and he has written scores for film, dance and theatre, including the Oscar-winning short West Bank Story. Since 1990, when he composed binaural music for the Monroe Institute, he has worked with neuroscientists, healers and spiritual teachers on music for meditation and wellbeing, and he founded the Metta Mindfulness Music label and the Inspired Sound Initiative, a non-profit offering arts programmes to young people.

His teaching draws on the sacred sound practices of several traditions: Sufi chanting and zikr, Kabbalistic and Hebrew prayer, Nada Yoga, Qi Gong's six healing sounds and Middle Eastern musical modes, alongside research on how sound affects the brain. He has taught at the Esalen Institute since 2009 and lectured at universities such as Yale, MIT, UCLA and Berklee. Divine Attunement: Music as a Path to Wisdom, a book of his with a foreword by Pir Zia Inayat-Khan, tells stories of mystics and musicians from many faiths and won an Indie Book Award in 2015. On The Shift Network he teaches a course on Sufi mystical sound traditions.
shamini-jain:
Dr. Shamini Jain is an American clinical psychologist, researcher and teacher whose work brings together scientific research and spiritual practice. She studied neuroscience at Columbia University, earned her doctorate in clinical psychology through the joint programme of the University of California, San Diego and San Diego State University, and completed postdoctoral training at UCLA. She is an adjunct professor in family medicine at UC San Diego and founded the Consciousness and Healing Initiative, a non-profit that brings scientists, practitioners, educators and artists together to study the biofield and the practice of healing.

Alongside her research she trained in energy work with Rev. Rosalyn Bruyere and draws on the Jain, Vedic and Tantric traditions. Her teaching combines short summaries of the research with guided meditation, mantra, chanting and voice work, and she often uses sound and song, having released an album, Kaliyuga Blues. Sounds True published her book on the biofield, Healing Ourselves: Biofield Science and the Future of Health. She has taught at Esalen, the Omega Institute and the Sivananda Ashram in the Bahamas, and teaches self-paced courses online through The Shift Network.
